questions.question: What limitation of ordinary next-token prediction motivates multi-token prediction?
options: It gives each position supervision for only one immediate future token
It requires a separate tokenizer per layer
It cannot be trained with cross-entropy
It prevents the use of shared embeddings
questions.explanation: Standard autoregressive training supervises each hidden state on exactly one next token. The lesson argues that this leaves longer-range structure to be learned indirectly instead of giving denser predictive signal from the same sequence.

questions.question: Why can't Gloeckle-style parallel MTP heads be directly reused as speculative-decoding drafts?
options: They predict from independent heads on the same hidden state without a causal chain between depths
They require a different vocabulary for each future offset
They only work with encoder-decoder models
They remove the LM head entirely
questions.explanation: Parallel MTP predicts several offsets at once, but those predictions do not condition on each other. Without that causal chaining, the model cannot naturally roll depth-1 output into depth-2 prediction the way a speculative draft needs to.

questions.question: How does DeepSeek-V3 form the hidden state for prediction depth k in sequential MTP?
options: By averaging all previous LM heads together
By combining the previous-depth hidden state with the embedding of the next-depth token, then passing that through module k
By discarding the backbone hidden state and starting from zeros
By running a separate tokenizer over future offsets
questions.explanation: Sequential MTP explicitly feeds forward a refined hidden state from the previous depth along with the embedding of the next token. That preserves an autoregressive-style causal chain across depths instead of making each future offset independent.

questions.question: Which expression matches the lesson's joint MTP loss?
options: L_MTP = λ × max_k L_k
L_MTP = Σ_k k × L_k with no normalization
L_MTP = (λ / D) × Σ_k L_k added on top of the main LM loss
L_MTP = CE(logits_1, logits_2) only
questions.explanation: Each prediction depth contributes its own cross-entropy term. The lesson averages those depth losses and scales them by λ before adding the result to the usual next-token objective.

questions.question: What is the two-part payoff of MTP in DeepSeek-V3?
options: Denser training supervision and a ready-made speculative-decoding draft at inference
Smaller vocabularies and longer pre-training context
Elimination of MoE routing and DualPipe
Deterministic decoding and zero KV cache
questions.explanation: During training, MTP gives each hidden state more than one target and improves the learning signal. At inference, the trained MTP module can be reused as a draft network, which the lesson says yields 80%+ acceptance and around 1.8x throughput gain.
